correctness.rationale: Every source word has a singleton letter and is primitive. The two repeated BWT entries correspond to rows beginning with the two successors. Direct first-letter-block sorting handles nonadjacent copies; lexicographic ordering of the two a-starting rows handles adjacent copies. Both yield exact iff adjacent ranks. There are (n-3)! necklaces per fixed repeated symbol and successor pair, yielding the exact two counts. Complete source-necklace and independent LF-cycle enumeration agree through n=9.

evidence: Theorem 3 of Fici et al. proves existence, and their counting theorem gives a lower bound for a specified ternary family, not an exact answer for growing support.
Kumallagov Proposition 5.5 counts all one-cycle last columns of given Parikh type before imposing full unclustering.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A general existence theorem and a general unrestricted one-cycle count do not imply the run-refined subset count. The known universal factor-two BWT clustering bound is likewise too weak to force the adjacent-successor criterion or exact counts.

exact_database_or_table.reasoning: Individual short-length values could be covered by finite BWT datasets. The claimed new fact is a uniform length-independent structural classification and closed formula, and neither inspected table gives or implies that all-n statement.

originality.rationale: The inspected primary sources give existence, generalized de Bruijn classifications, unrestricted Parikh one-cycle counts, and minimum input-run bounds but not the all-n fixed-content (2,1,...,1) unclustered-run distribution or its successor-order equivalence. The structural statement is not implied by the baseline because it imposes an additional adjacency predicate on last-column positions. An unindexed equivalent remains a residual priority risk.
residual_risks: A prior all-length treatment of near-permutation BWT run counts might exist under different terminology or outside indexed primary literature.
Fixed-length computer censuses could already include particular small instances; novelty is not claimed for any single finite row.
The ambient alphabet grows with n; this result does not resolve fixed-alphabet questions.

value.rationale: This is a natural full classification of the first nontrivial fixed-content case beyond a permutation word, motivated by the worst-case BWT clustering problem and explicit published open counting questions. It gives a structural iff, exact all-length numerator and denominator, and an asymptotic probability as support and length grow. The high-alphabet limitation is explicit and not presented as a fixed-alphabet result.
